research_rationale:
Whole-lifecycle YES claim for EO 12556 (Mailing Privileges of Members of Armed Forces of the United States and of Friendly Foreign Nations, April 16, 1986, 51 FR 13205), read in full from the held Federal Register text. The order has two operative sections and nothing else: section 1 delegates to the Secretary of Defense the function conferred on the President by 39 U.S.C. 3401(a) of designating an area for free mailing privileges, and section 2 requires the Secretary, when performing that function, to consult the Secretary of State, the Postal Service and other agencies and to give the Postal Service timely notice of designations and terminations of designations. Neither section carries a date, a condition, a report deadline or any own-terms end, and the order contains no revocation or supersession of another instrument. No later instrument amending, revoking or superseding the order is held: the packet chain has no events, the later-events OFR catalog search recorded 0 disposition notes naming it, and the held U.S. Code release point 119-121 prints the order's text as a note to 39 U.S.C. 3401 with no ending statement. The underlying statute still gives the President the designation function (held text of 39 U.S.C. 3401(a)(1)), so the delegated function has not lapsed with its authority. The U.S. Code edition is current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted after that date and on or before 2026-10-14 are not reflected in it); that limit is stated, not filled.
